en.title: Words that name
en.summary: Nouns and pronouns name people, places, things and ideas, or stand in for them.

paragraphs: A noun names a person, a place, a thing or an idea. A pronoun stands in place of a noun, so that we do not repeat it. Together they fill the subject and object places in a sentence.

English nouns change for number (book, books) and for the possessive (Maria's book). Pronouns change much more. They show person, number, gender and case: I, me, my, mine. A pronoun must match the noun it replaces.

blocks.html:
NounPronoun that replaces it
the teachershe or he
the bookit
the booksthey
Tom and Iwe
Maria's carhers

paragraphs: Names of particular people and places, such as Leeds and Maria, are proper nouns and begin with a capital letter. Words such as city and girl are common nouns and use a capital only at the start of a sentence.
Use he and she for people, and it for things and animals. Use they for a plural, and also for one person whose sex is not known or not stated.

items: Wrong: **The books is on the table.** Right: **The books are on the table.**
Wrong: **Maria she lives here.** Right: **Maria lives here.**
Wrong: **I saw he.** Right: **I saw him.**

ro.title: Cuvinte care denumesc
ro.summary: Substantivele denumesc ființe, lucruri sau locuri, iar pronumele țin locul unui substantiv.

paragraphs: Substantivul denumește o persoană, un loc sau un obiect. Pronumele ține locul unui substantiv deja menționat. Folosim pronumele pentru a nu repeta cuvintele.

În limba română, substantivele au trei genuri: masculin, feminin și neutru. Substantivele își schimbă forma la singular și la plural. Pronumele se acordă în gen și număr cu substantivul înlocuit. Adesea, pronumele subiect nu este obligatoriu în propoziție.
